This Miscellaneous First Appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, praying to modify the judgment and award dated 05-03-2021 passed by the Senior Civil Judge and MACT at Challakere in M.V.C.No.58/2018 by enhancing the compensation which is just and reasonable having regard to the facts of the case by allowing this appeal,
in the interest of justice and equity.

This Miscellaneous First Appeal coming on for Admission,
through Physical Hearing/Video Conferencing, this day, the Court delivered the following:
 JUDGMENT

The present appeal is filed by the claimant under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Court of the learned Senior Civil Judge and Motor Vehicles Accident Claims Tribunal, at Challakere, (hereinafter for brevity referred to as "the Tribunal"), in its judgment and award dated 05-03-2021, in M.V.C.No.58/2018.
2.

entities.text: Senior Civil Judge and Motor Vehicles Accident Claims Tribunal, at Challakere
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The summary of the case of the claimant before the Tribunal was that, on the date 26-05-2016, at about 7:30 a.m., while he was going on a Motor Cycle bearing registration No.KA-16/L-2898 from Renukapura to Basapura, as a pillion rider, a Tractor and Trailer bearing registration No.KA-16/T-9222/T-23, being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, came from the opposite direction and dashed to the Motor Cycle, in which the claimant was a pillion rider.
Due to the said road traffic accident, the claimant sustained grievous injuries to his legs and all over his body.

Immediately, he was shifted to the Government Hospital, Challakere, and from there to SSIMS-SPARSH Centre for Accidents, Bone and Joint Care, Jnanashankara, Davanagere, where the Doctor noticed that the claimant had sustained comminuted fracture on his left leg.

entities.text: SSIMS-SPARSH Centre for Accidents, Bone and Joint Care, Jnanashankara
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He was surgically operated.
He was treated as an in-patient in the Hospital for nearly thirty six days and has spent more than a sum of `5,00,000/- towards medical expenses.

The claimant has stated that at the time of the road traffic accident, he was hale and healthy and was earning a sum of `20,000/- per month from his work, however, due to the injuries suffered by him and the disability, he is not able to do his work as earlier.

With this, he has claimed compensation of a sum of `20,00,000/- with interest at the rate of `12% per annum, from the respondents No.1 and Shivananda H vs United India Ins.Co.Ltd on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195756031/
2 2, arraigning them as the owner and insurer of the alleged Tractor and Trailer respectively.

sentences.text: 3. In response to the notice served upon them before the Tribunal, both the respondents appeared through their counsels and filed their statement of objections, wherein they have denied the alleged manner of occurrence of the road traffic accident.
They have blamed the rider of the Motor Cycle for the alleged road traffic accident.

Further, the respondent No.2 therein - Insurance Company has also taken a contention that at the time of the accident, the driver of the Tractor and Trailer did not have a valid and effective driving licence to drive the said Motor vehicle.

4. Before the Tribunal, the claimant got himself examined as PW-1 and also got examined one Dr.
Chennareddy as PW-2 and got marked documents from Exs.P-1 to P-189.

On behalf of the respondents, respondent No.1 (owner) herself got examined as RW-1 and an Officer of the second respondent therein - Insurance Company got examined as RW-2 and two documents in the form of copy of the Insurance Policy and MLC extract were got marked as Exs.R-1 and R-2 respectively and the commissioner's report was got marked as Ex.C-1.

5. Though both the respondents entered the witness box and examined themselves as RW-1 and RW-2 respectively, however, the respondent No.1 (owner) in her evidence, admitted that, despite there being a specific direction by the Court to produce the Driving Licence of the Driver of the Tractor and Trailer at the time of the road traffic accident, she has failed to produce the same.

Per contra, the Officer from the respondent No.2 - Insurance Company, who was examined as RW-2 reiterated in his evidence that, the driver of the offending Tractor and Trailer had no valid and effective Driving Licence, as at the time of the occurrence of the road traffic accident.

The Tribunal, after holding that the respondent - Insurance Company could able to prove that the driver of the offending Tractor and Trailer was not having a valid and effective Driving Licence as at the time of the occurrence of the road traffic accident, though held the Insurer as liable to pay the compensation awarded by it, however, it reserved liberty to the Insurance Company, to recover the deposited amount from the respondent No.1 before it, i.e. the owner of the offending Tractor and Trailer.
6.

After analysing the evidence and the materials placed before it, the Tribunal has awarded the compensation under the following heads with the sum shown against them:

6 Loss of income during laid up 6,000-00  period
7 Loss of future income 1,61,280-00  Total 3,41,280-00 7.

The Tribunal has awarded a compensation of a sum of `3,41,280/- with interest at the rate of `9% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of deposit,
holding the owner and Insurer jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation and directed the Insurer to deposit the award amount, however, it reserved liberty to the Insurer to recover the deposited amount from the owner of the offending vehicle.

It is against the said judgment and award passed by the Tribunal,
the claimant has filed this appeal, seeking enhancement of compensation.
8. The learned counsel for the appellant (claimant) and the learned counsel for respondent No.1 (Insurance Company) before this Court are physically appearing before the Court.
On a memo filed by the learned counsel for the appellant, notice to Respondent No.2 (owner of the offending vehicle) is dispensed with vide order dated 01-08-2022.

9. Though this appeal is listed at the stage of admission, however, with the consent of the learned counsels for the parties, the same is taken up for its final disposal.
10.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that, he has the certified copies of the pleadings, depositions and exhibits, as such, summoning of the Trial Court records is also not required and that he would place those copies before the Court.
With this, he places the copies of the pleadings, depositions and exhibits for a perusal and their return to him.
11. In the light of the above, heard the arguments from both side.

Perused the materials placed before this Court including the memorandum of appeal, impugned judgment and also the certified copies of the pleadings, depositions and exhibits placed before the Court by the learned counsel for the appellant.

12. The present appeal being the claimant's appeal and the respondent Insurer having not preferred either cross-objection or a counter appeal, the question of occurrence of the road traffic accident on the date, time and place as alleged by the claimant and also the alleged rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending Shivananda H vs United India Ins.Co.Ltd on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195756031/
4 vehicle is not in dispute.

sentences.text:
Further, the claimant, who got himself examined as PW-1, apart from reiterating the contentions taken up by him in his claim petition even in his examination-in-chief also, has also got produced and marked documents from - 10 - Exs.P-1 to P-12, which inter alia includes the certified copy of the FIR, complaint, scene of offence panchanama, motor vehicle inspector's inspection report, wound certificate, charge sheet and discharge summary, which goes to establish the occurrence of the road traffic accident on the date,
time and place as mentioned in the claim petition and the claimant sustaining injuries in the said accident, so also the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the alleged offending Motor vehicle Tractor and Trailer bearing registration No.KA-16/T- 9222/T-23, in causing the said road traffic accident.
Thus, the only question that remains for consideration is, whether the claimant is entitled for any enhancement in the compensation awarded by the Tribunal in the matter.

13. The learned counsel for the appellant (claimant) in his argument submitted that, though the claimant did not produce any documents to establish his income at a sum of `20,000/- per month,
however, the Tribunal should - 11 - have taken the notional income of the claimant at a sum of `9,500/- per month, which was the prevailing notional income for the relevant year of the occurrence of the year of accident.

However,
the Tribunal has taken only a sum of `6,000/- per month as the notional income of the claimant, as such, the same requires to be enhanced by this Court.

He further submitted that the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards pain and sufferings, loss of income during the laid-up period, is also on the lower side and requires to be enhanced.

14. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 herein - Insurance Company, in her brief argument submitted that, the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal being just, fair and reasonable, does not warrant any interference at the hands of this Court.

She further submitted that, the rate of interest awarded by the Tribunal which is at `9% per annum on the compensation amount is also on the higher side and as such, the same requires to be reduced to `6% per annum.

. The evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 Doctor that, in the road traffic accident, the claimant sustained fractured injury is further corroborated by the documentary evidence such as wound certificate at Ex.P-6 and the discharge summary at Exs.P-8 to P-10.

The same would go to show that the claimant had sustained an open fracture of left tibia shaft which the Doctor diagnosed as a compound Shivananda H vs United India Ins.Co.Ltd on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195756031/
5 fracture of left tibia.

entities.text: Shivananda H vs United India Ins.Co.Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He has also sustained an abrasion near the fractured area on the left leg.

The discharge summary issued by the SSIMS-SPARSH Centre for Accidents, Bone and Joint Care,
Davanagere, would further go to show that, the injured was surgically operated and the procedure followed was ORIF with plates and screws.

entities.text:
SSIMS-SPARSH Centre for Accidents, Bone and Joint Care,
Davanagere
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: For more than a month, he was shown to be as an in-patient in the said Hospital from various dates from the date 26-05-2016 till the date 21-11-2016.
Thus the claimant should have suffered severe pain and sufferings due to the injuries sustained by him.
The Tribunal has awarded compensation of a sum of `25,000/- towards pain, trauma and sufferings on account of the - 13 - injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.

In the circumstances of the case, I am of the view that the same is slightly on the lower side and deserves to be enhanced by another sum of `10,000/-,
thus making it in total a sum of `35,000/- under the said head.
16. Towards the heads 'food and nourishment', 'conveyance charges' and 'attendant charges', the Tribunal has awarded a compensation of a sum of `10,000/- each.

Considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the claimant and the treatment undergone, I am of the view that the said compensation awarded under the said heads is just and reasonable, warranting no modification by this Court.
17. The claimant has contended in his evidence as PW-1 that, he was an experienced agricultural labourer and was earning a sum of `20,000/- per month.
Admittedly, he has not produced any documents to corroborate his income.
The respondents have denied the said income of the claimant.

In the absence of any - 14 - corroborative evidence, the Tribunal, though decided to take the notional income as the income of the claimant, however, in the said process it has taken a sum of `6,000/- as the notional income of the claimant at the time of the accident.

Since majority of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunals in the State have been taking a sum of `9,500/- for the relevant year 2016 as the notional income, the Tribunal ought to have taken a sum of `9,500/- per month as the notional income of the claimant.

Since the Tribunal has not considered the said notional income for the compensation towards the alleged future loss of income, the same requires recalculation in the light of the notional income taken at a sum of `9,500/- per month.
The claimant has contended that the injuries suffered by him have made him permanently disabled and unable to function as he was doing earlier.

In his support, he got examined one Dr.
Chennareddy as PW-2, which Doctor is an orthopedic surgeon, who, in his evidence has stated - 15 - Shivananda H vs United India Ins.Co.Ltd on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195756031/
6 that, he has examined the injured in the post operational period and has assessed his disability at 46% to the leg.

entities.text: Shivananda H vs United India Ins.Co.Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Admittedly, the said Doctor was not a treating Doctor and that he has not given the detailed calculation or the reasoning for arriving at such a percentage of alleged disability of the claimant.

However, considering the fact that the claimant had sustained a compound fracture to a weight bearing limb and that the Doctor has opined that there is some disfunction of the organ resulting in disability to the claimant, the Tribunal has considered the percentage of disability at 14% to the whole body of the claimant.

Since the Tribunal assessing the said disability at 14% to the whole body, though appears to be slightly on the higher side, I do not want to modify the same, that too, particularly when the respondents have not objected to the same by filing any cross objections to the appeal filed by the claimant.
Admittedly, the age of the claimant was 34 years as on the date of the road traffic accident, as could be seen - 16 - from the medical records.
Thus, the multiplier applicable for the said age is '16'.
Hence, the quantum of compensation for which the claimant is entitled to towards future loss of income would be a sum of `2,55,360/- (i.e. `9,500/- x 12 months x'16' multiplier x14/100).

After deducting a sum of `1,61,280/- awarded by the Tribunal under the said head, the claimant/complainant is entitled for a sum of `94,080/- which is the differential amount as an enhancement under the said head.
18. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of `6,000/- towards loss of income during the laid-up period.

Considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the claimant and the surgical operation he has undergone with plates and screws and also the organ for which the injury was sustained, I am of the view that he must have been laid-up for a period of not less than three months which has disabled him to do any work.
As such, he is entitled for a period of three months towards loss of income during the laid-up period, that too, at the rate of `9,500/- per - 17 - month, which is his notional income.

Thus the claimant would be entitled for a compensation of a sum of `9,500/- x 3 months = `28,500/- less a sum of `6,000/- awarded by Tribunal = `22,500/-,
which is the differential amount towards enhancement under the said head.
19.
Due to the injuries suffered by him, which has resulted into a permanent disability to some extent, the appellant must have been deprived of some amenities and comforts in his life.
But the Tribunal has failed to award any compensation under this head.

As such, towards loss of amenities and comforts in life, he is entitled for a sum of `10,000/-.
20.
Barring the above, the claimant is not entitled for compensation under any other heads or for any modification or enhancement of compensation under any other existing heads.

22. Though the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 herein - Insurance Company, in her argument vehemently contended that, the rate of interest awarded - 19 - on the compensation amount, which is at `9% per annum is on the higher side and requires to be reduced to `6% per annum, however, considering the fact that challenging the rate of interest, the respondent No.1 herein - Insurance Company has not preferred any appeal or cross objection and also considering the facts and circumstance of the case, occurrence of the year of the road traffic accident and the total quantum of compensation awarded, I find no reason to modify the rate of interest ordered by the Tribunal.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
[i] The appeal filed by the claimant stands allowed in part;

[ii] The impugned judgment and award passed by the learned Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal at Challakere, dated 05-03-2021, in M.V.C.No.58/2018, is - 20 - hereby modified to the extent that the compensation awarded by Tribunal at `3,41,280/- is enhanced by a sum of `1,36,580/- (Rupees One Lakh Thirty Six Thousand Five Hundred and Eighty only), thus fixing the total compensation at `4,77,860/- (Rupees Four Lakhs Seventy Seven Thousand Eight Hundred and Sixty only).
[iii] The rest of the order of the Tribunal with respect to fixing the liability upon the respondents and directing the respondent No.1 herein - Insurance Company to deposit the awarded amount, and reserving liberty to the respondent No.2 before it,
i.e. the Insurance Company (respondent No.1 herein) to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle (respondent No.2 herein), rate of interest awarded,
terms regarding release of the amount awarded shall all remain unaltered.
- 21 - Draw the modified award accordingly.

Since the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal at a sum of `3,41,280/-
is in short by a sum of `1,36,580/-, for the said enhancement of a sum of `1,36,580/-
only, the impugned judgment and award deserves to be interfered with.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
[i] The appeal filed by the claimant stands allowed in part;

[ii] The impugned judgment and award passed by the learned Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal at Challakere, dated 05-03-2021, in M.V.C.No.58/2018, is - 20 - hereby modified to the extent that the compensation awarded by Tribunal at `3,41,280/- is enhanced by a sum of `1,36,580/- (Rupees One Lakh Thirty Six Thousand Five Hundred and Eighty only), thus fixing the total compensation at `4,77,860/- (Rupees Four Lakhs Seventy Seven Thousand Eight Hundred and Sixty only).
[iii] The rest of the order of the Tribunal with respect to fixing the liability upon the respondents and directing the respondent No.1 herein - Insurance Company to deposit the awarded amount, and reserving liberty to the respondent No.2 before it,
i.e. the Insurance Company (respondent No.1 herein) to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle (respondent No.2 herein), rate of interest awarded,
terms regarding release of the amount awarded shall all remain unaltered.
- 21 - Draw the modified award accordingly.
Registry to transmit a copy of this judgment to the concerned Tribunal, without delay.
